Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No documented integration of the electoral register with the national data exchange layer. DE2030 does not specifically mention electoral data integration.

revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score is out of date. The cited Digital Ethiopia 2030 document indeed does not mention electoral integration, but the National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) launched, on 5 January 2026, a web- and mobile-based voter and candidate self-registration system ("Mirchaye") that authenticates users against Fayda national digital ID data, running alongside continuing manual/assisted registration. This is a genuine, operational integration between the electoral register and the national ID/data-exchange ecosystem. Score revised from 0 to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Since January 2026, Ethiopia's National Election Board (NEBE) has operated a web- and mobile-based voter and candidate self-registration system ("Mirchaye") that draws on Fayda national digital ID data for identity verification, running alongside continuing manual and assisted registration at polling stations ahead of the 7th General Election. This represents partial integration of the electoral register with the national identity/data exchange ecosystem.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No documented integration of employment registries or labor market information systems with the national data exchange layer confirmed.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score is only partly supported: no integration with the national data exchange is confirmed operational, but this is not wholly undocumented either. Ethiopia's Ministry of Labor and Skills (MoLS) runs a standalone Ethiopian Labour Market Information System (E-LMIS, marketed as the Bequ App) with its own biometric "Labour ID" for job-seekers and overseas workers, separate from Fayda. A September 2023 World Bank stakeholder engagement plan for the Ethiopia Digital ID project explicitly commits MoLS to "collaborate with NIDP on enrollment of job-seekers... on the Fayda system and use Fayda-based authentication for service delivery," but no subsequent source confirms this has been implemented. Score revised from 0 to 2 (Planned) on the strength of this single, now-dated World Bank planning document; flagged for human review as the evidence is thin and stale (2023) and the actual implementation stage is uncertain.
revised_comments: Ethiopia's Ministry of Labor and Skills operates a standalone Ethiopian Labour Market Information System (E-LMIS, also marketed as the Bequ App) with its own biometric Labour ID for job-seekers and overseas workers. Under the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project, the Ministry has committed to collaborate with the National ID Program to enrol job-seekers on the Fayda system and adopt Fayda-based authentication for service delivery, but integration of employment services data into the national data exchange remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No documented integration of court records or case management systems with the national data exchange layer. Justice digitization not specifically referenced in MESOB or EeGIF documentation.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score is out of date. Federal Supreme Court Directive No. 25/2025 (effective 3 October 2025) established an Electronic Filing and Litigation System (eFLS) that requires litigants and lawyers to authenticate using their national ID number to file cases and attend virtual hearings, alongside an Integrated Case Management System covering 24 federal court branches (with plans to extend to regional courts). This is genuine, operational integration between the justice system and national identity-verification infrastructure, though it is currently confined to federal courts and does not extend to correctional services or legal aid data. Score revised from 0 to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Since October 2025, Ethiopia's Federal Supreme Court has operated an Electronic Filing and Litigation System (eFLS) under Directive No. 25/2025, requiring litigants and lawyers to authenticate using their national ID number to file cases and attend virtual hearings. An Integrated Case Management System covers 24 federal court branches, with plans to extend to regional courts. This constitutes partial integration of the justice system with national identity-verification infrastructure, though correctional services and legal aid data are not yet covered.

The Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy commits to a "DE2030 Dashboard," annual progress reports, and Digital Transformation Council oversight as accountability mechanisms, but these remain forward-looking commitments — no public dashboard specifically covering data exchange operations or data-sharing agreements has yet launched. The Global Digital Identity Index separately confirms Ethiopia's dedicated data governance institution remains only "planned/in progress" and does not publish a progress report. Score of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) confirmed as of mid-2026; Value Name label mismatch noted in the original flag is cosmetic only.
revised_comments: Ethiopia's Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy commits to future accountability mechanisms, including a public dashboard, annual progress reports, and Digital Transformation Council oversight, but no public dashboard specifically covering data exchange operations or data-sharing agreements has yet launched. Independent tracking via the Global Digital Identity Index confirms that Ethiopia's dedicated data governance institution remains only planned or in progress and does not yet publish a progress report, indicating limited public disclosure regarding data exchange governance.
